Some background:

A major bank like this (4th largest in the country) is deemed a critical financial infrastructure to our country, and as such is required to have very carefully planned Disaster Recovery plans, including hot back up operations sites.

The back up hot sites are required to be at different physical locations miles apart from each other, sometimes in different states, so that in the event of a devastating earthquake or tornado or fire, or hurricane, etc, a disaster hitting one plysical location operation site, the primary site, it will not impact the back up hot site, and vice versa.

Hot Site = a back up site, many miles away physically from the primary operations site, that is maintained with parallel system processing, so that if the primary site experiences a disaster, the backup HOT SITE, immediately gets switched to ON. This is in contrast to a cold site which would require some start up time before it could be used. A back up HOT SITE should be operational, and running parallel 24/7, at least data wise...staff would have to travel to the back up site. That is the theory.
